item.title: NHL Shockwaves: Babcock Drama, Landeskog's Triumph, and a Wild Cup Final
item.description:
What if the most explosive NHL story of June 2026 wasn’t happening on the ice? Between a controversial coaching candidacy in Edmonton, a fairytale comeback in Colorado, and a Stanley Cup Final no one saw coming, the league is generating headlines faster than fans can refresh their feeds.

Quick Summary

  • The Edmonton Oilers are reportedly nearing a deal to hire Mike Babcock as head coach — and the NHLPA wants a full investigation first.
  • Gabriel Landeskog of the Colorado Avalanche won both the Masterton Trophy and the Mark Messier Leadership Award after his injury comeback.
  • The Carolina Hurricanes trail the Vegas Golden Knights 2-1 in the Stanley Cup Final, with Brandon Bussi now the starting goalie for Game 4.
  • The 2026 NHL Draft could see Gavin McKenna go No. 1 overall to the Toronto Maple Leafs.

The Babcock Bombshell: Why Edmonton Is Walking Into a Storm

According to ESPN, the Edmonton Oilers are nearing a deal with Mike Babcock to become their next head coach. For general manager Stan Bowman, the logic is straightforward: the Oilers’ core is in win-now mode, and Babcock owns a Stanley Cup ring and an Olympic gold medal.

item.title: San Jose Sharks Playoff Hopes Fade as Five-Game Losing Streak Bites Hard
item.description:
San Jose Sharks Playoff Hopes Fade as Five-Game Losing Streak Bites Hard

After spending most of the 2025–26 season firmly in the Western Conference playoff conversation, the San Jose Sharks are watching their postseason dreams slip away at the worst possible time. A brutal five-game losing streak has left the team scrambling with just weeks remaining in the regular season.

Key Takeaways

  • The Sharks sit at 32-31-6 (70 points), five points behind Nashville for the second wild card spot.
  • A five-game winless skid has derailed a season that exceeded preseason expectations.
  • Key injuries to Tyler Toffoli, Ryan Reaves, and others have thinned the lineup at the worst time.
  • With only 14 games remaining, every point matters — and the margin for error is nearly gone.

So how did a team that surprised the hockey world end up on the outside looking in?

item.title: Utah Mammoth Lock In Nick Schmaltz with Massive $64 Million Extension
item.description:
The Utah Mammoth just made one of the biggest moves of the NHL season, and it signals exactly where this franchise is headed. By locking in Nick Schmaltz to an eight-year, $64 million contract extension, the Mammoth have removed one of the league’s top pending free agents from the open market and planted a flag for long-term competitiveness in Salt Lake City.

Key Takeaways:

  • Nick Schmaltz signs an 8-year extension worth $64 million ($8 million AAV)
  • The Mammoth hold 73 points through 65 games in their second season since relocating from Arizona
  • GM Bill Armstrong continues an aggressive roster-building approach
  • Utah plans to be aggressive in the summer trade market, particularly targeting centers
  • Defenseman Mikhail Sergachev returns to the lineup after missing over a week

The Schmaltz Deal: Breaking Down the Numbers

The contract, announced on Wednesday, March 11, carries a cap hit of $8.0 million per season over eight years. For a forward who was set to become an unrestricted free agent this summer, the deal represents a significant commitment from both sides.
